title: SDK: Diagnostic hint codes and resumable-stream repair recipes
creator: Marcus Rivera
description: Problem: SDK clients (Python/TS/Go) surface low-level transport and runtime failures in inconsistent ways. Customers see opaque stack traces or generic 'internal_error' messages that provide no remediation path. Streaming sessions are particularly painful: clients either restart the whole stream or attempt naive retries that cause duplication or missed tokens. Goal: define a minimal, cross-SDK surface of diagnostic hint codes, structured error fields, and a resumable-stream repair recipe with per-language examples so developers can build deterministic recovery logic and give users actionable guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact 'diagnostic_hint' enum that appears on all non-2xx SDK exceptions with at least: TRANSIENT_NETWORK, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTION, KVCACHE_MISS_CORRUPTION, PARTIAL_STREAM_CHUNK, PROTOCOL_DESYNC, AUTH_EXPIRED, RATE_LIMITED

Add structured fields on exceptions: code (string), http_status (int as string), diagnostic_hint (string), retryable (true|false as string), suggested_action (short string), resume_token (string when applicable)

Implement resumable-stream protocol in Python/TS/Go SDKs: client generates idempotency/checkpoint tokens, server may return resume_token on PARTIAL_STREAM_CHUNK or PROTOCOL_DESYNC, and SDK provides helpers to resume at the last stable token

Ship language examples and README snippets demonstrating: exponential backoff with hint-aware early bailouts, safe deduplication when resuming, and user-facing error messages that suggest concrete next steps
Add CI tests that simulate common transient failures and assert the SDK surface exposes the diagnostic_hint and resume_token consistently across languages
Document mapping between runtime/server error codes and SDK diagnostic_hint values in a central Confluence doc and link to SDK changelogs
tasks: Draft diagnostic_hint enum and exception schema (design doc)
Review schema with API and runtime teams for compatibility
Implement error adapter layer in each SDK to translate server error envelopes into language exceptions
Add resumable-stream client helpers: CheckpointManager, ResumePoller, and safe-merge utility
Write language-specific README examples (Python, TypeScript, Go)
Create unit and integration tests simulating PARTIAL_STREAM_CHUNK and KVCACHE_MISS_CORRUPTION
Coordinate with runtime to return resume_token and diagnostic_hint for known failure modes
Publish RFC and announce to SDK users, include migration guide
technical_notes: Use a compact string-based 'code' (e.g., 'ERR_KV_CORRUPT') to avoid tight coupling to numeric codes
Treat 'resume_token' as an opaque base64 string produced by the server; clients must only attach it to resume requests

Retry policy should consult diagnostic_hint: for RESOURCE_EXHAUSTION use linear backoff with max attempts 3; for TRANSIENT_NETWORK use exponential backoff up to 5 attempts; for PROTOCOL_DESYNC do not auto-retry without resume_token
Streaming helpers must provide a 'drain-and-checkpoint' API: drain current in-flight chunks, persist last_committed_token, then attempt resume
Backward compatibility: SDKs must gracefully fall back if server does not return diagnostic_hint (treat as TRANSIENT_NETWORK for network errors, INTERNAL for others)
Telemetry: attach diagnostic_hint to SDK logs/metrics (tag: sdk.error_hint) and increment user-visible counters for each hint to help product prioritize fixes
